heuristics.statement: For a uniformly chosen trial coin rho_0 in F_p^* and starting point x_0 in F_p, the trail generated by the 795-operation step function F_rho0(x) on the origin-shifted BBLP 2-round affine input line W_rho0(x) = (rho0 * x - d0) mod p satisfies the success probability lower bound of Lemma 3 (P_succ >= 0.390002412759 >= 0.39) derived for a uniform random mapping on F_p.
heuristics.scope: Applies to the Lemma 3 random-mapping lower bound P_succ >= 1 - sum_{i=1}^8 e_i = 0.390002412759 >= 0.39 for the iterated walk x_t = F_rho0(x_{t-1}) with independent uniform trial coins (rho0, x0) in F_p^* x F_p, at the parameters of Section 3.3 (Delta = 2^141.775, n, d, G, MCAP = 29135, WG = 119, K = 22).
heuristics.extrapolation: Extrapolates single-trial distinguished-point collision behavior of the 795-operation r = 55 step function F_rho0(x) on the origin-shifted BBLP 2-round affine input line W_rho0(x) = (rho0 * x - d0) mod p from the executed reduced widths w in {10, 14} to the full 255-bit prime field F_p across 61 algebraic rounds (degree 5^61). The bound exceeds 0.39 by 2.41e-06, so the premise needs the fixed map's success to be within about 6.2e-06 (relative) of the random-function value.
heuristics.limitations: Reduced-width truncation tests low-bit projections of the full-field permutation rather than full 255-bit field collisions (which require ~2^126.21 compressions and are computationally infeasible to execute directly); random-mapping behavior at full width remains a standard cryptographic heuristic rather than an unconditional theorem. The filed budget tolerates a relative success deficit of about 6.2e-06 only: it carries essentially no robustness margin, exactly like the published r = 56 entries.

heuristics.statement: The compiled 19,017-instruction, 346-register, 337-constant register-machine program accurately implements the 795-operation multiplicative-coin step function, online rho0-constant scaling, 142-bit value / 119-bit gap bit-packing, single-segment DP recovery, and fifth-root message reconstruction within 1,048,548 bytes and W primitive operations.
heuristics.scope: Applies to the Section 4 register-machine compilation, memory accounting (1,048,548 bytes <= 1 MiB), and worst-case operation ledger (W = 135,190,572,559,388,628,633,764,944,186,046,286,039,627 primitive operations).
heuristics.extrapolation: The instruction-level interpreter executes the exact 19,017-instruction, 346-register, 337-constant program with full 255-bit field arithmetic, Theorem 1 online rho0-constant scaling, 142-bit value / 119-bit gap bit-packing, single-segment DP recovery, and fifth-root message reconstruction; only the walk horizon and output projection hook are scaled to w = 10 so collisions terminate within the 20-second organizer container budget.
heuristics.limitations: Direct end-to-end execution is performed at reduced walk horizon S = 69 (w = 10) rather than full-width S approx 1.6936 x 10^38 steps.
